description: RC3 / FR4 — raise the per-item context ceiling to 8192 across BOTH layers so the end-to-end ceiling actually works, HARD-GATED on a measured post-fix sweep. Layer 1: OVMS graph max_length (graph.pbtxt + model-pull --max_length). Layer 2: OmniRoute app guard OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS (default 4096, currently UNSET on the deploy). Depends on FEAT-001 being healthy (an 8192 ceiling is meaningless until the serving path serves within the readiness budget). Both layers MUST always carry the SAME number. 8192 is the user's final decision (not 12k, not a fallback) but is UNPROVEN on this GPU, so it is gated: regenerate the graph on ONE replica, sweep up to ~8192 tokens, and only raise both layers if an ~8192-token input returns 200 within budget.
steps: Confirm FEAT-001 left a stable healthy majority (re-check pods READY, no climbing restarts). Capture the current graph max_length on a healthy pod (expect 4096 before this feature).

Regenerate the OVMS graph to max_length 8192 on ONE replica via the partitioned roll (reuse the FEAT-001 partition mechanism: set partition to the highest ordinal). Use the non-destructive in-place mechanism: update the model-pull initContainer args in ~/sources/kube/omniroute-memory/ovms-embeddings-statefulset.yaml to --max_length=8192 and ensure the graph is regenerated with 'ovms --configure --model_path /models/OpenVINO/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-int8-ov --task embeddings --pooling LAST --truncate=true --max_length 8192 --target_device GPU' (fallback --overwrite_models). NO PVC wipe. Apply and let only the top-ordinal pod roll.
Verify on that rolled pod: kubectl -n omniroute-memory exec <pod> -c ovms -- grep max_length /models/OpenVINO/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-int8-ov/graph.pbtxt reads 8192.

Run a token-size sweep against that replica up to ~8192 tokens (repeated-word input, curl -w %{time_total}, generous -m). Record HTTP code and latency per size. PASS = ~8192-token input returns HTTP 200 AND latency is within a client-acceptable budget; because 4096 already costs ~32 s, treat >60 s as a FAIL.

On PASS: set the OmniRoute guard to MATCH — kubectl -n omniroute set env deploy/omniroute OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS=8192 (no sudo needed; live patch is the source of truth). Then lower the partition stepwise so the remaining replicas roll with --max_length=8192, waiting for each to hold READY. Reset partition to 0 after.

On FAIL (8192 too slow or errors): step down by powers of two (8192 -> 6144 -> 4096; 4096 is already proven to serve) and pick the largest that passes the budget. Set BOTH layers to that proven value (graph + OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS). Then call send_message with severity 'warning' escalating the gap-to-8192 to the user (they asked for a larger window; the GPU could not serve 8192 within budget) — do NOT silently downgrade.

Leave OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_ITEM_OVERFLOW at its default 'auto' (external callers get HTTP 400 naming the over-cap item; internal callers get truncation+warning). OVMS does NOT truncate over-length input, so 'auto' is the only truncation backstop.

For the declarative record of the OmniRoute env change: create a fresh .bak of ~/sources/kube/omniroute/omniroute.yaml and reconcile the env in the file. NOTE the BLOCKER: omniroute.yaml is root-owned and passwordless sudo is unavailable — if the file cannot be written, the live kubectl env change is authoritative; report the file reconcile for the user to finish (do not block the live change on it).
acceptance_criteria: The configured per-item ceiling is identical at both layers: OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS equals the OVMS graph max_length (target 8192, or the proven-serving fallback if 8192 fails the gate) (design AC5).
An input AT the configured ceiling returns HTTP 200 within the probe/client budget on a healthy replica (the F2 gate was run and its result recorded in findings).
An input ABOVE the ceiling is cleanly rejected per the auto policy (external caller -> HTTP 400 naming the item and the cap).
The live graph.pbtxt reads the configured max_length after rollout.
If 8192 failed the gate, the user was escalated via send_message (warning) rather than silently downgraded.
verification: ssh ... 'kubectl -n omniroute-memory exec <healthy-pod> -c ovms -- grep max_length /models/OpenVINO/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-int8-ov/graph.pbtxt' — reads the configured value (8192 or proven fallback).
ssh ... 'kubectl -n omniroute get deploy omniroute -o jsonpath="{..env[?(@.name==\"OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS\")].value}"' — equals the graph max_length.
Public API: an input at the configured ceiling -> HTTP 200 within budget; an input above it -> HTTP 400 naming the item (auto policy).
ssh ... 'kubectl -n omniroute-memory get pods -l app=ovms-embeddings' — all replicas READY on the new graph, no climbing restarts.
findings:
FEAT-003 (2026-10-09) — COMPLETED. 8192 FAILED the F2 gate; user decided 4096 at BOTH layers.

FINAL APPLIED CEILING: 4096 at BOTH layers.
- Enforced OmniRoute guard: OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS=4096 (FEAT-001 set it live; confirmed, not thrashed). OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_ITEM_OVERFLOW=auto (left as instructed).
- OVMS graph max_length: 4096 on ALL 4 host-native PF nodes (10.1.1.12/13/14/15) — lowered from 8192, reconciled ONE node at a time behind nginx failover (edit graph.pbtxt + systemctl restart ovms-embeddings-host, per-node .bak kept, each verified serving 1024-dim before the next). NixOS module modules/ovms-embeddings-host.nix maxLength binding set 8192->4096 with rationale comment, committed isolated on branch dev (commit e2057f6, .bak kept, flake/SR-IOV drift untouched, NOT pushed).
- GRAPH max_length at completion: 4096 (live on all 4 PF nodes AND in the committed NixOS module).

VERIFICATION (all pass): all 4 host graphs read max_length: 4096; guard reads 4096 (both layers SAME number); public API small input -> HTTP 200 + 1024-dim; over-ceiling single item -> clean HTTP 400 naming item/cap (overflow=auto); OVMS-side over-cap now rejects AT 4096 (observed 'Input length 5002 longer than allowed 4096'); qdrant untouched (gen=1, uid a2c81b89-45b7-407c-bd5b-691eceb47aa8). Local workspace docs reconciled: LIVE-VERIFICATION.md + ovms-embeddings-statefulset.yaml header now state max_length=4096 at both layers; deploy-report.md has a FEAT-003 section with the sweep table and decision.

FOLLOW-UP for a larger window: GPU driver/firmware fix D (i915-sriov-dkms / GuC-HuC bump) + source-side embedding concurrency cap. 4096 is the proven-stable operating point on this MTL Arc PF hardware.

--- GATE EVIDENCE ---
8192 FAILED the F2 gate; escalated to user.

TOPOLOGY NOTE: FEAT-001 moved embeddings OFF the in-cluster StatefulSet (now scaled to 0, partition=3, zero pods) onto a HOST-NATIVE OVMS podman service on each gremlin PF Arc device (10.1.1.12-15:8000), fronted by the ovms-embeddings-proxy nginx Deployment. So the FEAT-003 'regenerate the graph on ONE StatefulSet replica via the partition' step was moot: there is no StatefulSet replica to roll, and the host-native graph was ALREADY built at max_length=8192 (verified on all 4 PF nodes: graph.pbtxt reads max_length: 8192). The F2 sweep was therefore run against the real host-native PF path, which is the only live embeddings serving path.

F7 RE-VERIFY (fresh, this session):
- STS ovms-embeddings: replicas=0, partition=3, NO pods (scaled to 0 by FEAT-001).
- Host-native graph max_length on all 4 PF nodes (10.1.1.12/13/14/15): 8192.
- OmniRoute guard OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS=4096 (ENFORCED); OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_ITEM_OVERFLOW=auto; OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=12288.
- Reranker mem limit=12Gi. qdrant sts 1/1, 10d, untouched.
- Layers DISAGREE today: graph=8192 (unenforced headroom), guard=4096 (enforced). FEAT-003 requires both to carry the SAME number.

F2 TOKEN SWEEP (host-native PF, gremlin-4 then gremlin-1, repeated-word input, POST /v1/embeddings):
| input words | HTTP | time_total | note |
| 100  | 200 | 4.46 s | |
| 1000 | 200 | 0.64 s | |
| 2000 | 200 | 1.44 s | |
| 4000 | 200 | 7.95 s | |
| 6144 | 200 | 13.19 s | largest power-of-two step that PASSES the <60s budget on an IDLE backend |
| ~7900 (near 8192 cap) | 000 | >90 s TIMEOUT | GPU WEDGED; did not return within 90s on a healthy backend |
| 8192 words (~8194 tok) | 400 | 14.3 s | over graph cap: 'Input length 8194 longer than allowed 8192' (hard reject, truncate:true does NOT clip) |
After the near-ceiling sweep, gremlin-4 (healthy 0.87s ping before) went to a 12s ping timeout = WEDGED, matching FEAT-001's documented ccs0 fence-timeout wedge under sustained large-item compute.

F2 GATE RESULT: FAIL at 8192. A near-8192-token single item does not return within the >60s FAIL threshold (>90s, wedges the Arc GPU). This independently reproduces FEAT-001's finding (single ~8192-tok item = 30-300s + GPU wedge), which is why FEAT-001 deliberately set the enforced guard to 4096.

PUBLIC-API over-ceiling check (overflow=auto, external caller): a single large item returns a clean HTTP 400 naming the item/estimate/cap with split guidance ('over the 4096-token per-item limit for arc-embed; split the input or set OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_ITEM_OVERFLOW=truncate'). Overflow left at 'auto' as instructed.

FALLBACK CANDIDATES (step down from 8192 by powers of two, pick largest that passes budget):
- 8192: FAIL (wedge / >90s).
- 6144: PASSES an idle-backend latency sweep (13.2s < 60s), BUT raising the ENFORCED guard 4096->6144 is a user-visible behavior change on a shared live cluster: it would admit 6144-token single items that cost ~13s idle and demonstrably push the Arc PF into the wedge regime under real concurrent load (the exact failure mode FEAT-001 mitigated down to 4096).
- 4096: proven-serving and the current ENFORCED guard; FEAT-001's proven-stable operating ceiling.

FINAL APPLIED CEILING: PENDING user decision (escalated via send_message warning). The behavior-preserving reconcile is to set BOTH layers to 4096 (lower the unenforced graph headroom 8192->4096 to MATCH the enforced guard; no caller sees a change because the 4096 guard already rejects larger single items). The only safe larger option (6144) carries live-stability risk and is a product decision, not a mechanical step-down.

Graph max_length at time of this feature: 8192 (host-native, unenforced). Will be reconciled to the chosen value once the user answers.
